title: Market Mogul: Stock & Business Empire
description: Navigate the thrilling world of Indian stock markets and business investments. Build a financial empire from a modest inheritance by making smart investment decisions.

scenes.title: The Inheritance

choices.label: I should visit a financial advisor first and get proper guidance before doing anything
choices.description: Seek professional guidance before making any decisions

choices.label: I'm excited — let me open a Demat account right away and jump into the stock market
choices.description: Jump into the stock market headfirst with excitement

scenes.narrative: Your grandfather, a retired banker from the State Bank of India, has left you ₹10 lakhs in his will along with a handwritten letter: 'Money sleeping in a savings account is money wasted. Make it grow, but grow wise first.' You stand outside his old house in Kolkata, letter in hand, thinking about your next move.

scenes.title: The Advisor's Office

choices.label: I'll spread my money across stocks, bonds, and mutual funds to stay safe and grow steadily
choices.description: Spread investments across stocks, bonds, and mutual funds

choices.label: I want to go all in on high-growth stocks — bigger risk but the returns could be amazing
choices.description: Concentrate on companies with high growth potential

scenes.narrative: You visit a SEBI-registered financial advisor in Park Street. Her office walls are decorated with charts and a framed photo with Rakesh Jhunjhunwala. She studies your inheritance details and smiles. 'Ten lakhs is a good start. The question is: what kind of investor do you want to be?'

scenes.title: The Trading Floor

choices.label: I'll start with trusted blue-chip companies like TCS and Reliance — safe and proven picks
choices.description: Start with established companies like TCS, Reliance, and HDFC

choices.label: I'll hunt for cheap penny stocks that could explode in value — high risk, high reward
choices.description: Look for cheap stocks with explosive growth potential

scenes.narrative: You walk into a bustling brokerage office near Dalal Street. Screens flash green and red. Traders shout orders. The energy is electric. A friendly broker sees your wide eyes and approaches. 'First time? Don't worry, everyone starts somewhere. The Sensex is on a bull run - perfect timing!'

scenes.title: Your Journey Begins
scenes.narrative: With your first investment decisions made, the real game begins. The Indian markets are volatile, opportunities are everywhere, and every choice will shape your financial future. Your grandfather's letter sits on your desk as a daily reminder: grow your money, but grow wise first.

npcs.name: Anita Desai
npcs.personality: Sharp, fast-talking, slightly aggressive, deeply connected to market pulse
npcs.backstory: 15 years on Dalal Street. Started as a floor runner, now one of Mumbai's top brokers. She has seen three market crashes and made money in each one. Her instincts are legendary but her advice comes at a premium.

npcs.name: Ravi Kumar
npcs.personality: Smooth, persuasive, always has a deal, patient long-term thinker
npcs.backstory: Built a real estate empire starting from a single plot in Gurugram. Believes land is the only real wealth. Known for turning abandoned areas into premium commercial zones. His projects span from Mumbai to Bangalore.

npcs.name: Prof. Arun Chakraborty
npcs.personality: Academic, thoughtful, cautious, sees the big picture, sometimes overly theoretical
npcs.backstory: IIM Calcutta professor who moonlights as a financial commentator on CNBC Awaaz. His students include several CEOs and fund managers. He believes in fundamental analysis and distrusts market hype.

competitors.name: Cautious Carl
competitors.chat_personality: Conservative investor who values safety over high returns. Quotes Warren Buffett frequently. Prefers index funds and fixed deposits. Will warn you about risky moves.

crisis_events.title: Market Crash!
crisis_events.description: The Sensex drops 2000 points in a single day! Global recession fears and FII pullout trigger panic selling. Your portfolio is bleeding red. What do you do?

choices.label: Sell everything
choices.description: Cut your losses and move to cash before it gets worse
choices.feedback: You sold at the bottom. Classic panic selling. Within weeks, markets recovered and you missed the bounce-back. A costly lesson in emotional investing.

choices.label: Hold your positions
choices.description: Stay calm and ride out the storm like a seasoned investor
choices.feedback: Diamond hands! Markets recovered within a month. Your portfolio bounced back and your patience was rewarded. As Buffett says, 'Be fearful when others are greedy.'

choices.label: Buy more at lower prices
choices.description: Invest additional cash while stocks are cheap
choices.feedback: Bold move! Buying during a crash is contrarian but historically profitable. When markets recovered, your new purchases gave excellent returns. Your grandfather would be proud.

crisis_events.title: Insider Information!
crisis_events.description: An old college friend now works at a major pharma company. He whispers that they're about to announce a breakthrough drug. 'Buy before the news breaks,' he says. But insider trading is illegal under SEBI regulations.

choices.label: Act on the tip
choices.description: Buy the pharma stock before the announcement
choices.feedback: The stock soared 40% after the announcement. But SEBI's surveillance system flagged unusual trading patterns. You got lucky this time, but insider trading carries prison time and heavy fines. Is it worth the risk?

choices.label: Report to SEBI
choices.description: Do the right thing and report the insider information
choices.feedback: You reported the tip to SEBI. Your integrity earns respect in the financial community. SEBI's investigation leads to action against the insider. Ethical investing pays off in reputation and trust.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.description: Thank your friend but don't act on it and don't report it
choices.feedback: You stayed out of trouble. The stock did go up, but you avoided legal risk. Sometimes the best investment decision is the one you don't make.

crisis_events.title: Cryptocurrency Craze!
crisis_events.description: Bitcoin has hit a new all-time high and everyone from auto drivers to IIT graduates is talking about crypto. Your social media is flooded with crypto influencers promising 100x returns. RBI's stance remains cautious.

choices.label: Invest 20% in crypto
choices.description: Diversify into Bitcoin and Ethereum through an Indian exchange

probability_outcomes.feedback: Crypto rally continues! Your Bitcoin investment doubles. But remember, what goes up can come crashing down. This is not a long-term strategy.
The crypto market crashed 40% overnight. Your investment lost significant value. The 30% TDS on crypto transactions makes it even worse. Speculative investments are dangerous.

choices.label: Study blockchain technology instead
choices.description: Learn about the technology before investing any money
choices.feedback: You spend weeks understanding blockchain, DeFi, and Web3. This knowledge helps you identify genuine blockchain companies listed on NSE. Education before investment is always wise.

choices.label: Stay away completely
choices.description: Stick to regulated markets and traditional investments
choices.feedback: You avoid the crypto rollercoaster entirely. While some friends made money, many lost their savings. Your regulated portfolio continues steady growth. Discipline beats FOMO.

base_rounds.title: First Investment Decision
base_rounds.story: Your Demat account is set up, KYC is done, and ₹10 lakhs sits in your trading account. The market is open. Nifty 50 is at an all-time high. Business channels debate whether it's a bubble or genuine growth driven by India's digital transformation. What's your first major move?
base_rounds.goal: Make your first significant investment decision

choices.label: Start SIPs in mutual funds
choices.description: Begin systematic investment plans in diversified equity mutual funds via SIP of ₹50,000/month
choices.feedback: Smart and disciplined! SIPs average out market volatility through rupee cost averaging. Over time, this is how most Indian wealth is built. AMFI data shows SIP investors outperform lump-sum investors 70% of the time.

choices.label: Buy individual stocks
choices.description: Research and pick specific companies to invest in directly on NSE/BSE
choices.feedback: You bought shares in IT and banking stocks. Initial gains are exciting but individual stock picking requires deep research and constant monitoring. Not all stocks in your basket will be winners.

choices.label: Fixed deposits and bonds
choices.description: Put money in bank FDs and government bonds for guaranteed returns
choices.feedback: Safe and predictable. Your FD at SBI gives 7% annual returns. Government bonds add stability. But with inflation at 6%, your real returns are barely positive. Playing it too safe has its own risks.

base_rounds.image_prompt: a bustling stock exchange floor filled with traders at their desks, screens displaying soaring stock prices, bright lights illuminating the excitement, tension palpable in the air
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Time ran out! Indecision has consequences — you lost ground on key metrics.

base_rounds.title: The IPO Opportunity
base_rounds.story: A major Indian tech company is going public. The IPO is the talk of the town - from Dalal Street to your neighbourhood chai stall. The company has strong revenues but has never turned a profit, similar to many global tech IPOs. Grey market premium is sky-high. Everyone you know is applying.
base_rounds.goal: Decide whether and how to participate in a hyped IPO

choices.label: Apply for maximum allocation
choices.description: Submit the highest bid to maximize your chances of allotment

probability_outcomes.feedback: IPO listed at 90% premium! Your allotment turned into instant profit. Listing day gains are exciting but remember - not all IPOs perform well post-listing. Many fall below issue price within months.

The stock listed at a modest premium but crashed 30% within a week as institutional investors dumped their shares. IPO hype doesn't always translate to value. This is why SEBI mandates a cooling period.

choices.label: Apply with a small amount
choices.description: Invest a modest sum to participate without overexposing yourself
choices.feedback: Conservative IPO participation is a smart strategy. You get exposure to the listing without betting the farm. Win or lose, the learning experience is valuable.

choices.label: Skip the IPO entirely
choices.description: Wait for the stock to settle post-listing before evaluating
choices.feedback: Patient approach. You study the company's quarterly results after listing before making a decision. Post-IPO price often corrects to fair value within 6 months. Value investors prefer this approach.

base_rounds.image_prompt: a bustling Indian marketplace with vibrant stalls, people animatedly discussing stock prices, colorful banners announcing the IPO, warm afternoon sunlight casting lively shadows

base_rounds.title: Real Estate vs Markets
base_rounds.story: Ravi Kumar, the real estate mogul, approaches you with a deal: a pre-launch apartment in Whitefield, Bangalore at ₹45 lakhs - 20% below market rate. Meanwhile, Anita is pushing you towards a promising mid-cap portfolio. Prof. Chakraborty warns that putting too many eggs in one basket is dangerous. You can only pick one major investment.
base_rounds.goal: Choose between real estate and stock market investment

choices.label: Buy the Bangalore apartment
choices.description: Invest in Ravi's pre-launch property deal with a combination of cash and home loan
choices.feedback: You secured a prime Whitefield property. Indian real estate has historically appreciated 8-12% annually in tech hubs. But liquidity is low - you can't sell a flat as easily as stocks. EMI payments begin next month.

choices.label: Build a mid-cap portfolio
choices.description: Follow Anita's advice and invest in high-potential mid-cap stocks on NSE

probability_outcomes.feedback: Mid-cap stocks rally as India's manufacturing sector booms! Your portfolio outperforms the Nifty 50. Mid-caps can deliver 20-30% returns but carry higher volatility than large-caps.
Mid-cap selloff! FII outflows hit smaller stocks hardest. Your portfolio drops significantly. Mid-caps are high-risk, high-reward. Patience is key - these stocks often recover over 2-3 year cycles.

choices.label: Split between REIT and index fund
choices.description: Invest in a Real Estate Investment Trust and a Nifty 50 index fund for balance
choices.feedback: REITs give you real estate exposure without buying property, and index funds track the market. Prof. Chakraborty approves. This diversified approach reduces risk while capturing growth from both sectors.

base_rounds.title: The Business Opportunity
base_rounds.story: A friend from IIT proposes a business partnership: an AI-powered EdTech startup targeting Tier 2 and Tier 3 Indian cities. He needs ₹5 lakhs from you as co-founder investment. The business plan is solid but startups are inherently risky. Meanwhile, your portfolio manager suggests tax-saving ELSS funds before the March 31 deadline.
base_rounds.goal: Decide between entrepreneurial investment and tax-efficient investing

choices.label: Co-found the EdTech startup
choices.description: Invest ₹5 lakhs as a co-founder in the AI EdTech venture

probability_outcomes.feedback: The startup takes off! Within a year, 50,000 students in small-town India use your platform. A Series A investor values the company at ₹10 crore. Your equity is worth 20x your investment. But this outcome is rare - 90% of Indian startups fail.
The startup struggles with user acquisition and burns through cash. Your friend wants more investment. This is the reality for most startups - great ideas need great execution and timing.

choices.label: Invest in ELSS tax-saving funds
choices.description: Put ₹1.5 lakhs in ELSS mutual funds for Section 80C tax deduction
choices.feedback: Smart tax planning! ELSS funds give you equity exposure with a 3-year lock-in period and save up to ₹46,800 in taxes. The dual benefit of tax saving and market returns makes ELSS one of the best Section 80C options.

choices.label: Angel invest a small amount + ELSS
choices.description: Give ₹2 lakhs to the startup as an angel investor and put ₹1.5 lakhs in ELSS
choices.feedback: You diversify between entrepreneurship and tax planning. The smaller startup investment means less equity but also less risk. ELSS handles your tax obligations. A balanced approach to opportunity and prudence.

base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Time ran out! Indecision has consequences — you lost ground on key metrics.

base_rounds.title: Global Crisis Impact
base_rounds.story: A global banking crisis erupts. Major banks in Europe face collapse. FIIs pull ₹50,000 crore from Indian markets in a single month. The Rupee weakens against the Dollar. RBI calls an emergency meeting. Your portfolio is down 25% and your phone is buzzing with anxious calls from family asking if their money is safe.
base_rounds.goal: Navigate a global financial crisis and protect your wealth

choices.label: Shift to gold and sovereign bonds
choices.description: Move funds to safe-haven assets like Sovereign Gold Bonds and government securities
choices.feedback: Gold rallies during global uncertainty. Sovereign Gold Bonds offer 2.5% annual interest plus gold price appreciation, and they're tax-free on maturity. Your portfolio finds stability. In times of crisis, gold has been India's trusted haven for centuries.

choices.label: Aggressively buy the dip
choices.description: Use your cash reserves to buy quality stocks at rock-bottom prices

probability_outcomes.feedback: Legendary move! Markets recovered within 6 months and your crisis-bought stocks delivered 40-60% returns. This is exactly what Rakesh Jhunjhunwala did in 2008. Courage during fear creates wealth.
The crisis deepened further. Your new purchases lost value too. Catching a falling knife is dangerous. The recovery took longer than expected and your cash reserves are now depleted.

choices.label: Stay the course with SIPs
choices.description: Continue your systematic investments without changing strategy
choices.feedback: Your SIPs buy more units at lower prices, reducing your average cost. When markets recover, these units will be worth significantly more. Discipline beats timing. Data shows SIP investors who stayed invested during 2008 earned 15%+ CAGR over 10 years.

endings.title: Warren Buffett of India
endings.description: Your financial acumen is the stuff of Dalal Street legend. From a modest ₹10 lakh inheritance, you built a diversified empire spanning stocks, real estate, and businesses. Financial newspapers feature your journey. Your grandfather's letter now hangs framed in your office - you fulfilled his dream and then some. SEBI invites you to speak at investor awareness programs.

endings.title: Steady Investor
endings.description: You may not have made headlines, but your portfolio has grown steadily and your financial knowledge is solid. You understand risk, you respect the markets, and your wealth compounds quietly. You start a weekend financial literacy workshop in your community. Slow and steady wins the race.

endings.title: Smart Saver
endings.description: You prioritized capital preservation over aggressive growth. Your cash reserves are healthy and your risk is minimal. While others chased multi-baggers and lost sleep, you built a stable financial foundation. Your FDs and bonds provide steady income. Not glamorous, but secure.

endings.title: Lessons Learned
endings.description: Your investment journey had its ups and downs. Some bets paid off, others didn't. But the most valuable thing you gained is financial literacy. You now understand market cycles, risk management, and the power of patience. Your grandfather's letter reminds you: the real wealth is wisdom. Your next decade of investing will be much better.

random_events.text: Bonus dividend declared! One of your blue-chip holdings announced a special dividend of ₹20 per share. Cash flows in!
Income Tax notice received! Short-term capital gains tax demands arrived. STCG at 15% on equity profits held less than 1 year.

how_to_play: You inherited ₹10 lakhs and must build a financial empire through smart investment decisions. Every choice affects your Portfolio Value, Cash, Market Knowledge, Risk Level, and Reputation.
Talk to NPCs for expert advice: Anita Desai for stock picks, Ravi Kumar for real estate opportunities, and Prof. Chakraborty for economic insights. Their advice is free but not always unbiased.
Watch for hidden outcomes! Some investments have uncertain results - just like real markets. High-risk choices may use hidden deltas with probability-based outcomes.
Compete against Cautious Carl, an AI investor with a conservative strategy. Chat with him for a different perspective on your decisions. Can you beat his returns?
learning_objectives: Understand key financial instruments available in Indian markets: stocks, mutual funds, bonds, REITs, gold, and IPOs.
Learn the principles of diversification, risk management, and the relationship between risk and return.
Develop awareness of Indian financial regulations including SEBI guidelines, tax implications (STCG, LTCG, Section 80C), and ethical investing practices.
Appreciate the importance of financial literacy, patience, and disciplined investing over speculation and market timing.

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.

cultural_context: India's NSE is one of the world's largest stock exchanges by derivative volume. As equity investing becomes more accessible to Indian retail investors through platforms like Zerodha and Groww, market literacy is a vital skill for India's financial inclusion agenda.
reflection_prompt: How did you adapt as the AI shifted strategies? Which adaptation worked best?
